entry.dc:title: All-Purpose Ventilation Jet Unit for Deep Open Pit Mines.
entry.dc:creator: Bukhman Y.
entry.dc:description: An all-purpose ventilation jet unit based on the latest model of the turbojet engine RD-3M-500 motor truck, is described. It is marked by increased output, flexibility of control of the jet trajectory, universality and self-contained operation. The flow of air in the jet is 298 kg/s at the initial speed of 455 m/s. The capacity of the unit is 40,000 h. p. and its size is 9 multiplied by 4 multiplied by 4 m. The unit is suitable for an open pit mine 200 m deep, 1000 m in diameter.

entry.dc:title: Effect of Open Pit Geometry on the Parameters of a Free Stream.
entry.dc:creator: Ushakov K.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: It is found that parameters of an air stream carrying out natural ventilation of an open pit mine depend on the geometry of the excavated space. On the basis of experimental and natural investigations, relations are proposed that permit determination of the quantity of air taking part in the ventilation of the open pit. Its depth and the slope angle of the leeward side are taken into account. The formulas derived make it possible to calculate more precisely natural ventilation in an open pit mine, taking into account its geometry and the specific features of the development of a free stream in the pit.

entry.dc:title: Environmental impact study. A tool for sound mineral development
entry.dc:creator: Ackerman D.H.
entry.dc:description: As a result of some 8 years of exploratory work the American Metal Climax Co. has ascertained that copper-molybdenum deposit located in northwest Wyoming, near an old mining camp of Kiroin has sufficient Cu-Mo mineralization to warrant its consideration as an open pit mined. Paper discusses the scope of an environmental impact study which will have to be completed with cooperation of local authorities before a final decision is taken. Some more significant elements of the study are: reclamation of the vegetation at the altitude of open pit from 8,000 to 11,000 ft; waste and tailings disposal in a high, narrow valley; water pollution by mine drainage and ore treatment plant; housing etc.

entry.dc:title: Influence of Climate on the Organization and Planning of Mining Works at an Open Pit Mine.
entry.dc:creator: Shpanskii O.
entry.dc:description: A method of calendar planning of monthly productivity of open-pit equipment and of the monthly volumes of drilling and blasting and excavation work, taking into account changes in the climatic conditions in the course of a year, is described. This method is appropriate for severe arctic conditions.

entry.dc:title: Overvoltages with Single-Phase Grounding in 6-10 kV Networks with an Insulated Neutral Wire.
entry.dc:creator: Volotkovskii S.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenij I Energeticheskikh Ob Edinenij Sng Energetika
entry.dc:description: The problem of the influence of inter-phase capacitance on overvoltage values in conditions of single-phase grounding in networks with an insulated neutral wire is considered. Methods are presented for determining the magnitude of inter-phase capacitance for the limitation of overvoltages in conditions of single-phase grounding. The influence of the limitation of overvoltages on the operation of protections against single-phase groundings is analyzed. Application in open pit mine electric networks is mentioned.

entry.dc:title: Calculation Basis for a New Method of Recording the Indices of the Transportation Systems of Open Pit Mines Using Automobile Transport.
entry.dc:creator: Selyanin V.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: A new method of recording the productivity of open pit mine dump trucks is considered. It is based on interrelation between the pressure in the hydraulic system of the tilting arrangement and the weight of the transported rock. The main design principles of the method are presented and the devices worked out on the basis of the stated principle are described.

entry.dc:title: Determination of a Rational Direction of Deepening an Open-Pit Mine by Graphs of Isolines of Specific Return.
entry.dc:creator: Zagoruiko G.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: A method is set forth for determining a rational direction of deepening an open pit mine by using the example of a deposit of silicate nickel ores in the Urals, characterized by a variety of forms and condition of bedding of ore bodies. The problem is solved by the method of variants in two stages. Plane problems are solved by means of geometric mine graphs of isolines of specific return. The spatial problem is solved by means of a longitudinal section of the pit on which the lines of the transverse sections are imposed, indicating the gain at the level of the calculated horizons when lowering the mining operations in accordance with the rational direction found for the plane problem. The variants of the pit deepening are evaluated by the summary reduced gain, taking into account the factor of time and the capital investment efficiency coefficient.

entry.dc:title: Automatic Stabilization of the Vibration Level of the Drilling Machines.
entry.dc:creator: Marasanov Y.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: A new principle of designing a systen of automatic control of the rasp drilling process is explained. The permissible (according to industrial hygiene norms) level of vibrations of the drilling machines is adopted as control criterion. In a particular case, the system can be adjusted to any capacity of the machine. The system realizes the most effective method of removing a machine from the vibration zone. Industrial tests of the system, carried out at the main open pit mine of the Kachkanarskig ore dressing combine, and maintenance experience have proved its efficiency and reliability.

entry.dc:title: Synthesis of Optimal Technological Schemes of Open-Pit Mine Workings.
entry.dc:creator: Lepilkin N.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: An attempt is made to formulate and to outline the ways of solving the problem of synthesis of optimal technological schemes of open pit mine workings using continuous action technology. On the basis of an analysis of the features of some of the main such technological schemes, a series of structural parameters are established, defining the class of the discussed technological schemes in an identical way. Introduction of structural parameters enables the synthesis problem to be reduced to that of nonlinear integer-value programming. A method is proposed for the determination of the optimum values of the parameters, based on the principle of self-instruction.

entry.dc:title: Field of Application of the Promising Types of Transportation in Deep Open Pit Mines.
entry.dc:creator: Novozhilov M.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: Dependence of the parameters of the working zone of an open pit mine, its productive capacity and the main technical and economic indices of the handling and transport equipment on the depth of the working zone and the plane size of the pit are considered. It is established that the dimensions of the pit and its working zone exert essential influence on the productive capacity and volume of technological shipments. For open pits of different length and form, the fields of application and parameters of promising types of transportation are determined.

entry.dc:title: BOUGAINVILLE.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Open pit mine and concentrator built by Conzinc Riotinto of Australia and New Broken Hill Cons. at a total cost of 426-million (see Ei 1970 p 719 Abs. #09484 and 12923) scheduled to mill 90,000 tpd of ore containing 0. 65% Cu and 0. 02 oz Au/ton started operation 6 mo. ahead of schedule. Issue contains monographic description of the mining and milling operations, inclusive of listing the equipment employed. Detailed flow sheets of the concentrator are shown. Concentrate is pumped through a 6 in. od pipeline over a distance of 17 mi to a filter and drying plant at the sea shore.

entry.dc:title: FUNCTIONAL OPTIMIZATION OF OPEN PIT MINE DESIGN UTILIZING GEOLOGIC CROSS-SECTION DATA.
entry.dc:creator: Luke K.
entry.dc:description: A computer programming system has been devised to assist in open pit mine design planning. This system operates upon data generated for cross sections in the mine plan, and parallels present manual methods used in mine design, resulting in a minimal communications barrier between the mine planner and the computer. Input data for each cross section includes geologic interpretation and mine design parameters such as wall angles, bench heights, berm widths, and ramping system. The program will optimize the design of each cross section to give minimum stripping at any desired ore reserve level.

entry.dc:title: GRADIENT CONTROL AT AN OPEN-CAST MINE
entry.dc:creator: MOBSBY CM
entry.prism:publicationName: J Inst Mine Survey S Afr
entry.dc:description: Article examines methods used for gradient control in an open pit mine with particular reference to an adjustable gradient indicator.

entry.dc:title: MARQUESADO, SPAIN'S PREMIER IRON ORE MINE FORGES AHEAD
entry.dc:creator: ANON
entry.dc:description: This large, producing 2 million tons/yr of hematite ore, open pit mine, located in southeastern part of Spain presents an interest in that it had switched from shovel excavator, rail transportation system to trackless method employing rubber tired front-end- leaxers and dumpers. Proved reserves are estimated to amount to 50 million tons of ore, assaying between 53 and 57% Fe. The shipping port at Almeria is 60 mi distant from the mine.

entry.dc:title: AITIK. WORLD'S FIRST THIRD GENERATION OPEN PIT COPPER MINE IN LAPLAN
entry.dc:creator: WYLLIE RJM
entry.dc:description: In Swedish Lapland about 30 mi north of Arctic Circle, the Boliden Company is producing 2,000,000 t/yr of copper ore, assaying 0. 5%Cu, from its Aitik open pit mine under harsh climatic condition. The sub-outcrop of the ore body, covered by glacial moraine overburden 6 to 40 ft thick, is about 6500 ft long and from 165 to 600 ft wide dipping about 25//0. Highly mechanised and automated mining and milling operations produce an overall productivity per employee of 20,000 t/yr thus assuring a profitable operation. Measures taken to allay cold weather problems are discussed.

entry.dc:title: PHELPS DODGE UNVEILS TYRONE. NEWEST SOUTHWEST COPPER MINE
entry.dc:creator: ARGALL G.
entry.dc:description: Located in Grant County, NMex, open pit mine is designed for 25,000 tpd of ore, assaying about 0. 80% Cu, thus adding 55,000 tons/yr of copper and solidifying Phelps Dodge Corp position as second largest copper producer in the United States. The primarily sulfidic orebody is located in a broken or faulted block in quartz monzonite stock, intruded into Precambrian granite. Mine is unusual in that, during its life, re will be hauled downhill to the mill. Mining is done with six electric shovels with 10 cu yd bucket. Ore and waste are hauled by fleet of 27 LectraHaul 85-ton trucks.

entry.dc:title: Metamorphic aspects of the magnetite-hematite deposit at Benson Mines, New York
entry.dc:creator: Hagni R.
entry.dc:description: The relationships between the iron oxide, sulfide, and silicate minerals were deter-mined in more than 500 polished sections and about 200 thin sections of Benson magnetite-hematite ore and host gneiss. The universal stage was utilized to determine the orienta-tion of those opaque ore minerals that have a unique physical direction and the determined ore abric was compared with that of biotite and sillimanite in the host gneiss. Rims of garnet, sillimanite, and plagioclase about the iron oxide and some sulfide grains, together with poikiloblastically enclosed iron oxide and sulfide grains in garnet and sillimanite, indicate that some of the opaque minerals were present at the time of formation of those silicate minerals. Similar microtextures show that part of the sulfide minerals, pyrite, pyrrhotite, and chalcopyrite, were present at the time of iron oxide crystallization. Other grains of those sulfide minerals form later veinlets that transgress the silicate, oxide, and earlier sulfide grains. ?etrofabric diagrams for the basal cleavage of biotite grains in thin sections of oriented specimens collected from the Benson open pit mine exhibit well the foliation that may be observed in the mine; the c-axes of sillimanite crystals commonly are aligned in a direction of lineation within the biotite foliation plane. ?etrofabric diagrams for the long axes of ovate ore grains exhibit more scatter than those of biotite and sillimanite, but the axes of such grains exhibit a tendency to lie within the biotite foliation plane and to be relatively concentrated in the direction of sillimanite lineation. This tendency is greatest in the more strongly foliated and lineated specimens. The writers interpret the ore microscopic, petrographic, and petrofabric results to indicate that metamorphism has played an important role in the development of the present nature of the Benson ores. © 1969 Society of Economic Geologists, Inc.

entry.dc:title: SOME DEVELOPMENTS IN POLISH OPEN PIT MINING
entry.dc:creator: ANON
entry.dc:description: In parallel with underground mining, during past ten yrs rapid development of opencast mining has taken place in Poland; at present nearly 200 million tons of ore and minerals are mined by opencast methods and approximately 150 million tons by underground mining; steadily increasing depth of mined mineral deposits, increasing productive capacity of single mine up to 50 million t/yr and introduction of large capacity belt conveying are main developments illustrated in case of sulfur open pit mine near Tarnobrzeg in Central Poland, producing presently 400,000 t/yr of pure S and Turow mine, near Czechoslovakia and East German borders, producing 15 million t/yr of lignite, with installed total length of belt conveyors amounting to 100 km.

entry.dc:title: DESIGN OF OPEN PIT MINE SLOPES
entry.dc:creator: RANA MH
entry.dc:description: Surface mines operating in Canada's Sub-Arctic have developed slope design adapted to geological and climatic conditions of region; geology of Labrador Trough is discussed; samples of Ruth Slate and Quartzite, these being the two rock types which had been most in evidence in past failures, have been subjected to triaxial compression tests; developed in Soviet Union in 1966, L. F. Savkov's equation for determining slope stability has been applied to delineate potential failure planes for different slope angles with given slope height; practical conclusions are drawn.

entry.dc:title: Applied geology at the Nickel Mountain Mine, Riddle, Oregon
entry.dc:creator: CHACE FM
entry.dc:description: Nature of nickelsilicate ore deposit, its general geology, mineralogy, structure, rock alteration, chemistry, and origin, are all unique in North America. Applied geology activity consists of collection of geologic facts by open pit mine mapping, drilling and laboratory work, and use of geologic data in ore reserve computations, mine planning, grade control and study of special problems relating to mining, beneficiation, and smelter operation. Of these, nickel grade control is perhaps most important single aspect.
